jen: Heads up—seen a weird flurry of partial-JSON parse errors from customers using our SSE stream. Looks like auth token refresh + small chunk sizes is producing JSON objects split across data events. anyone fought this across go/python/js clients?

mike: yes. saw this in a demo yesterday. token refresh causes reconnects that cut mid-object if client is naively concatenating chunks. errors are usually `JSONDecodeError` or `unexpected end of JSON input`.

sasha: main strategies we've used: 1) NDJSON (one JSON object per line) so you can safely buffer until newline, 2) length-prefix framing inside the SSE data payload (e.g., `len
{json}`), 3) incremental parser (stateful) that can accept partial bytes. each has tradeoffs.

jen: NDJSON is appealing for compatibility but we can't change protocol for hosted tenants w/o rollout. Thinking about client-side fixes first. any simple incremental parser snippets?

mike: for python asyncio, the pattern that worked for us is to accumulate bytes and try loads only when we see a newline or closing brace heuristic. small snippet: 

```python
# naive incremental approach
buf = b""
async for chunk in resp.content.iter_any():
    buf += chunk
    while b"\n" in buf:
        line, buf = buf.split(b"\n", 1)
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        obj = json.loads(line.decode())
        handle(obj)
```

# caveats: only works if server emits newline-delimited JSON

jen: that's great if server uses NDJSON. But many streams are single JSON objects that update partial fields (we stream patches). how to handle split utf-8 bytes? saw decode errors when chunk cut between multibyte char.

sasha: always treat the buffer as bytes and decode only complete sequences. python's incremental decoder helps: `codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')`. keep bytes until decoder accepts them.

alex: for go, we used an incremental json decoder: `json.Decoder` can't handle partial top-level values across a stream unless you feed it an io.Reader that blocks until more bytes arrive. pattern: wrap the SSE data lines into an io.Pipe and write to the pipe as chunks arrive; `json.NewDecoder(pipeReader).Decode(&v)` will block until a full value is ready. avoids manual buffer management.

mike: example go pattern: 

```go
pr, pw := io.Pipe()
dec := json.NewDecoder(pr)
// reader goroutine: push SSE data payloads into pw.Write
// decode goroutine:
var obj map[string]interface{}
for {
    if err := dec.Decode(&obj); err != nil {
        // handle io.EOF / temporary errors
        break
    }
    handle(obj)
}
```

# note: must carefully close pipe on reconnects

jen: nice. what about backpressure? consumers get overwhelmed because we naively spawn goroutines/Tasks per chunk. need a flow-control pattern.

sasha: two options: 1) bounded work queue + worker pool, and pause reading from the socket when queue is > high-water mark, resume when below low-water mark; 2) use OS-level TCP backpressure by not reading from the socket (but that ties into event loop semantics in js/python).

mike: in node/browser streams you can use ReadableStream and call controller.enqueue and backpressure is applied automatically when consumer doesn't pull. server-sent events libs sometimes hide the underlying byte stream though.

alex: for go, you can stop reading from the net.Conn (or return from the Read loop) and that halts the kernel buffer growth. we implemented a semaphore: read loop acquires `sem` token; processing returns token. if no token available, read loop blocks.

jen: concrete ask: I'm going to open a small devex PR with helper utils for incremental parsing + a bounded processing queue for python and go clients. can volunteers review? low-risk, docs + tests.

mike: lgtm to review. can you also add an example for token-rotation reconnects? common failure: token refresh triggers reconnect while we still have partial bytes; need to clear buffers or signal decoder to reset.

jen: yes plan: on reconnect event, close any pipe/incremental decoder, drain/clear buffers, then resume fresh. will add explicit note about not reusing half-decoded state.

ci-bot: jen pushed commit 3e7b2a7 -> branch devex/sse-incremental.

jen: pinging @sasha @mike for review when you have a minute. I'll add unit tests that simulate split UTF-8 and mid-object token rotation.

sasha: I'll review tomorrow morning. quick checklist: tests for newline-delimited, length-prefixed, and arbitrary split-chunks; test backpressure behaviour (queue limits) and reconnect reset semantics. also add integration example for browser using ReadableStream.

mike: one more gotcha: when using fetch streaming in browsers, sometimes `response.body.getReader().read()` returns zero-length chunks; treat them as no-ops, don't attempt decode.

jen: good call. I'll include that. thanks all :pray:
